### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **67** of **249** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `da3ed1c44af051d266b3f7f56b029bdb2c49e001` — the merge of head `389fb46e219571655596be992a6e662d43e41b07` into base `8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin da3ed1c44af051d266b3f7f56b029bdb2c49e001 && git checkout da3ed1c44af051d266b3f7f56b029bdb2c49e001
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d 389fb46e219571655596be992a6e662d43e41b07 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d && git merge --no-ff 389fb46e219571655596be992a6e662d43e41b07

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8925d5bcb1a96beb59ff6ae35fada6f69f4f893d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**Shape and gates.**
- `l1-face --pr 36247` at 6979716525 is CLEAN (13 items).
- First line is `Fixes #34862`.
- Floors are success. Check-runs: 37 success, 16 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending. `mergeable_state` is clean.
- The changeset names `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` (patch).

**The code.**
- `consolePageLink` (`public-base-url.ts`) takes only the PATH of the auth service's `getConsoleUrl('/')`, which is `${origin}${uiBasePath}`. It keeps the approval links' own origin (`publicBaseUrl`). It drops a base path the two share, so a sub-path deployment is not prefixed twice.
- No composer, a throwing one, an empty answer, or a non-URL answer gives no mount, which is the link built before.
- The e-mail's `approvalUrl` and both action-link doors (`approval-service.ts` `handleActionPage` and the plugin's raw-app mount) build the inbox link through the same function, so the two doors still answer one page.
- `inboxHref` is escaped (`esc`).
- The plugin reads `auth` at link time, and a `getService` throw counts as no auth service.

**Pins and evidence.**
- Default `/_console` mount, root mount (`uiBasePath: '/'`), the inbox link under the same mount, and no auth service.
- Origin kept, shared base path, relative link with no base, and the four no-mount cases.
- The premise was measured on a real `os dev` boot: 404 before, 200 with the request open after (dev report 7073910032). That covers both mounts the card's premise named.

**R1 (must fix: the declaration). This is `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, not `no`.** The criterion (`execution-duties.md:75`) is "本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗". `ApprovalServiceOptions` is exported from the package entry (`src/index.ts:21`), and it gains an optional input member, `getConsoleUrl`. That enlarges the public surface. The changeset already says so in prose ("`ApprovalServiceOptions` gains the optional `getConsoleUrl`").
- Fix: rewrite the line-initial declaration to `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in both the PR body and the changeset, and name the new member on that line or beside it. That is a changeset-only commit, and I will read only that delta.
- After ACCEPT, the contract review goes to the seat for the widening.

**Not findings.**
- The link change for every default deployment (`/system/approvals` → `/_console/system/approvals`) is the fix itself, and the changeset states FROM → TO.
- The in-app `actionUrl` is unchanged.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `a6fcdc4060f02da16a3e74bcd24b7d16fde656af`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/action-link-pages.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/public-base-url.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approvals-plugin.ts, .changeset/34862-approval-link-console-mount.md + none
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

Face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and the changeset; no `packages/spec/src/**` and no governed path in the 7-path diff). Read: card #34862 and all its comments, PR #36247's body, file list and every comment (L1 7074126064 REWORK, 7074476331 ACCEPT included), `git diff origin/main...a6fcdc4060`, and the head's check-runs (`pr-state`: 37 success · 16 expected skip · 0 failed · 0 pending · `mergeable_state` clean). The dev report 7073910032 was read as a claim; each point below is checked against the code.

### ① Derived judgments

**Published surface.** The package's `exports` has only `"."`. `src/index.ts` is not in the diff. Of what the diff changes, it reaches only `ApprovalService`, `ApprovalServiceOptions` (`index.ts:18-21`) and `ApprovalsServicePlugin` (`:35`). `consolePageLink`, `ConsolePageComposer`, `APPROVALS_INBOX_PATH` and `renderResultPage` live in modules that no `exports` entry can address. They are shipped bytes, not the published accept set, so "no new export" (PR body) is true.

**Accept-set and public-surface changes, each against the declaration:**
- `ApprovalServiceOptions.getConsoleUrl?: ConsolePageComposer` (`approval-service.ts:2033`) is a new optional input member. The changeset (`:12`) and the PR body both declare it. It is a widening: every options object accepted before is still accepted, and leaving the member out gives the old e-mail link, because `consolePageLink` with no composer returns `publicBaseUrl + pagePath` (`public-base-url.ts:101-123`, pinned in `public-base-url.test.ts`).
- `approvalUrl` (`approval-service.ts:2574`) changes from `BASE/system/approvals?request=ID` to `BASE/_console/system/approvals?request=ID` under the auth composer's default mount. It stays `BASE/system/approvals?request=ID` under `uiBasePath: '/'`, or with no composer or no auth service. The changeset states this FROM → TO exactly. It is not a narrowing: the old link answered 404 on every boot this tree ships. `createConsoleStaticPlugin` mounts only at `CONSOLE_PATH = '/_console'` (`packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts:55`), and no source on this tree sets `uiBasePath` to anything but the `/_console` default (`git grep`). The new link follows the one setting the spec documents for this (`auth-config.zod.ts:612-621`), which is the same composer that every auth e-mail, OAuth page and invitation link already uses (`AuthManager.getConsolePageUrl`, `auth-manager.ts:5436-5452`). A host that builds `ApprovalService` by hand and passes no composer keeps its old link byte for byte.
- `actionUrl` (the in-app deep link): unchanged at `approval-service.ts:2567`. So `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx:1141-1143` ("`notify()` rewrites the inbox action URL to `/system/approvals?request=ID`, so clicking the bell opens that request's drawer") is still true. No hand-written doc states the e-mail link's or the action page's URL shape (`git grep` over `content/docs`, release pages excluded).
- The action-link page's inbox href (`ApprovalService.handleActionPage`, `approval-service.ts:8110-8140`; the plugin's raw-app door, `approvals-plugin.ts:566-584`) changes from the origin-relative `/system/approvals` to `consolePageLink(publicBaseUrl, composer, '/system/approvals')`. That gains the mount, and also the `publicBaseUrl` origin whenever one resolves. **The declaration does not state the second half, and two of its sentences are false about it: see F1.**
- `renderResultPage` gains an optional third parameter (internal module), and every caller passes it (`git grep`, 6 call sites). The two doors build the href through one function from the same `publicBase.url` and the same composer, so the claim that both doors answer the same bytes holds.

**Origin rule (#30509).** It is preserved. `consoleMountPath` (`public-base-url.ts:101-123`) takes only the PATHNAME of `composer('/')`, so the auth composer's own origin is discarded, including its `http://localhost:3000` fallback (`auth-manager.ts:5417`). A test pins this (`consolePageLink` "keeps its own origin"). The origin is still `resolvePublicBaseUrl`'s answer or nothing: with no base the link is relative under the mount. The shared-base-path strip also keeps a deployment that already set `publicBaseUrl` to `https://host/_console` on its old link (the mount equals the base path, so it is stripped).

**Security-touching: no.** No changed hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour. The auth service is read only for a URL path, and the action-token peek and redeem calls are untouched. The new href is `esc()`-escaped (`action-link-pages.ts:131`). The links open a page that already requires sign-in, and they decide nothing. **Rule-change-verified: none**, because no `.claude/**` path is in the diff.

**Findings**

- **F1 · should-fix · `.changeset/34862-approval-link-console-mount.md:12`** (the PR body's "What changes" bullet for `approval-service.ts` repeats it). The declaration's FROM → TO is not exact for the inbox link.
  - "The base is still the approval links' own (`publicBaseUrl` …)". The inbox link had no base: it was the origin-relative `/system/approvals` (main's `action-link-pages.ts`).
  - "A kernel with no auth service has no mount to read, and the links stay as they were." This is false for the inbox link whenever a base resolves. With no composer, or a composer that answers nothing (no auth service under the plugin, or a host that constructs `ApprovalService` without `getConsoleUrl`), the href goes from `/system/approvals` to `BASE/system/approvals` (`approval-service.ts:8139-8140`, `approvals-plugin.ts:270,566`). The PR's own pin asserts exactly that (`approval-service.test.ts:7300`).
  - Why it matters. This is a change in the published `handleActionPage`'s output: the link moves from the serving host to `publicBaseUrl`'s host. It is not a narrowing I can construct a loss for: the page is reached by an action link built under the same `publicBaseUrl`, and on a sub-path deployment the absolute form is the correct one. But the CHANGELOG line ships to npm and says the opposite.
  - Fix, changeset prose only, no code. State the inbox link's own FROM → TO: origin-relative `/system/approvals` → `BASE/_console/system/approvals`, absolute under `publicBaseUrl` when one resolves and relative when none does. Limit "stay as they were" to the e-mail link, and state that with no mount the inbox link is `BASE/system/approvals`. Mirror it in the PR body.
- **F2 · nit · `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.test.ts:7297`**. The title "the links are the ones built before" is false for its own second assertion (`:7300`, `${ORIGIN}/system/approvals`, where the link was `/system/approvals` before). Retitle it with F1, for example "…the e-mail link is the one built before and the inbox link carries the base".

Not findings:
- `ConsolePageComposer` is not exported from the root. A consumer types the member structurally as `(path: string) => string | undefined`, which is enough for an optional callback.
- `approval-email-templates.ts:30-32` (outside the diff) still reads "the request page under the deployment's public origin". It is incomplete now that the mount is added, but it is not false.

### ② Semver level

`patch` is right. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct: `ApprovalServiceOptions` is a runtime host option, not authorable metadata, and nothing under `packages/spec` moves. AGENTS.md:1022-1031 says a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`, and `none` takes `patch`. The member is optional, so no existing caller breaks. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the right arm: an optional input member added to an exported options type is a widening and not a narrowing. Only one changeset names the package, and it carries both declaration lines line-initially. That agrees with the PR body.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag: root mount pinned at service level only.** Accepted. No boot on this tree serves the Console at `/`: the only console-static factory mounts at `CONSOLE_PATH` (`console.ts:55`), its one caller is `serve.ts:5837`, and no source sets `uiBasePath`. The `/` case is therefore pinned at the service with the composer's exact composition (`approval-service.test.ts`, "under a root mount the e-mail link stays at the root"), and that is the most this tree can show. A host that serves the Console at `/` without setting `uiBasePath: '/'` gets a `/_console` link. That host is misconfigured under the spec's own setting, and its auth e-mails already point at `/_console`. The changeset states that the link follows `uiBasePath`, so this is declared and not a silent narrowing.
- **SQL push-down: n/a.** The diff adds no query, id materialisation or in-app join. It composes URL strings only.
- `open_questions` in the dev report: none. Author `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is needed.
- Out of scope, source-read only, not measured: `packages/services/service-messaging/src/slack-channel.ts:130-168` makes the Slack DM link as `deploymentOrigin()` plus the relative `actionUrl`, with no Console mount. This looks like #34862's defect on the Slack channel. It goes to a follow-up card through the filing gate, not to this PR.
- Gates: the head's check-runs are 37 success, 16 expected skip, 0 failed and 0 pending.
- Verdict: F1 (should-fix) is open, so this head does not land on this record. The rework is a prose-only delta (changeset, PR body, test title), and I will read only that delta.
